items.title: How does comment bluntness affect fix turnaround?
items.description: L1's two reviewers found the identical bug: a fully person-directed, vague, instruction-style comment took about 3 days (72 hours) to get a fix; a code-directed, specific, question-framed comment took about 20 minutes (0.33 hours). Drag the slider to see how turnaround scales between those two real endpoints as a comment gets blunter — the dashed line marks Reviewer A's actual 3-day outcome.

params.name: bluntness
params.label: Comment bluntness (0 = code-directed, specific, question — 100 = person-directed, vague, instruction)

items.compute: const best = 0.33; const worst = 72; const t = Math.pow(params.bluntness / 100, 1.6); const hoursToFix = best + (worst - best) * t; return { hoursToFix: Math.round(hoursToFix * 100) / 100 };

items.title: How many round-trips does an unlabeled batch cost?
items.description: L2's batch example showed an author fixing everything 'to be safe' when severity wasn't labeled, because they couldn't tell the one blocking bug from the seven nits. Model this as: the fraction of comments left unlabeled drives how many extra clarifying round-trips the author needs before landing the real fix, on an 8-comment batch like the one in the unit.
items.compute: const maxRoundTrips = 3; const roundTrips = (params.unlabeledPercent / 100) * maxRoundTrips; return { roundTrips: Math.round(roundTrips * 10) / 10 };
